_general.insight: Apostrophes inside a jq expression wrapped in bash single-quotes terminate the bash string. Contractions like "today's" silently break the hook. Avoid contractions in any `jq -nc '...'` block, or escape with `'\''`.

cli/describe.mjs.insight: When a CLI needs to find a user-installed binary (claude, node managed by nvm/asdf, homebrew tools), spawning `$SHELL -lc 'command -v <bin>'` is the universal lookup — it sources the user's interactive dotfiles, so it finds anything their terminal would. Plain `which` from a launchd-spawned or Finder-spawned process misses every shell-managed PATH.

Any spawned long-running child (claude --print, ffmpeg, anything that may hang) needs both an idle watchdog (no stdout for N seconds → SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period) and a wall-clock ceiling. `proc.on('exit')` alone is a foot-gun — the parent inherits the child's hang. Surface stderr live (clear the spinner line before each chunk) so a hung child still shows its diagnostic noise instead of going silent.

When parsing streaming LLM output across CLI versions whose envelope format may be either full-snapshot-per-turn or token-deltas, dedup at the *consumer* level (Set of already-emitted keys) instead of trying to detect which format the CLI is using. Append everything you see; the per-key Set makes re-processing identical text idempotent. JSONL output (one `{path, description}` per line) is far easier to incrementally parse than a single closing-brace JSON object.

cli/add.mjs.insight: `process.stdin.isTTY` is unreliable inside Claude Code's Bash tool — the agent wraps Bash in a pty, so isTTY returns true even though no human is there to type. Gate interactive prompts on three signals together: an explicit --yes flag, `process.env.CLAUDECODE === "1"` (Claude Code's documented env var), and the isTTY check. Always pair an interactive readline with a wall-clock timeout fallback so a misclassified non-interactive run can't hang forever.

components/LiveDescriptionsContext.tsx.insight: For a stable mutable slot across renders, use `useRef`, not `useMemo(() => ({}), [])`. StrictMode double-renders re-execute useMemo's initializer, so any "set once" object you stash there can be reset on the second pass — the bug only shows up in production after a user reload, not in dev. Reach for useMemo only when you actually want a memoized *computed* value tied to deps.

components/RepoSwitcher.tsx.insight: Index-based arrow navigation needs a client-side stable sort key — never lean on the order the backend happens to deliver. The daemon's repos() sorts by recency, so every agent touch reshuffles the list and a `(idx + 1) % n` next-pointer silently bounces between repos as activity churns. Backends are free to ship lists in whatever order suits them; the consumer that does positional traversal owns sort stability.
